title: Soft-migrate KV microsegments with probabilistic reclamation to reduce fragmentation
creator: Maya Chen
description: We observe increasing GPU-side KV cache fragmentation in dense, continuous-batching workloads. Fragmentation reduces usable contiguous regions and increases allocation failures under burst traffic, forcing expensive fallbacks to smaller model variants or degraded latency. This ticket designs and implements a soft-migration + probabilistic reclamation system that moves live KV entries to compact regions without pausing inference, reduces fragmentation over time, and integrates with the continuous batching scheduler to avoid SLO regressions.
proposed_design:
Overview:
- Introduce logical microsegments: fixed-size subregions within each KV pool (default 64KB granularity) tracked by a lightweight segment map. Microsegments are the unit for migration/compaction decisions (not individual tokens).

Soft-migration flow:
1) Identify candidate donor microsegments: segments with low live density or high external fragmentation score (free run-lengths within segment).
2) Select contiguous target segment(s) with enough free space to absorb migrated entries. For best GPU copy efficiency prefer contiguous target ranges on same GPU memory bank.
3) Quiesce affected entries via epoch markers: per-request kernel annotations capture the KV generation id used by that inference. Migration proceeds only when no in-flight requests reference the donor generation or migration is performed with copy-on-write semantics for hot keys.
4) Perform asynchronous GPU-device memcpy (cudaMemcpyAsync / P2P where available) to copy individual KV blobs into the target microsegment. Maintain a small redirection table (per-pool single-level indirection) mapping logical key -> physical microsegment + offset.
5) Atomically flip the redirection pointer. Old slot kept as tombstone until safe reclamation window passes (based on epoch and conservative request durations).
6) Reclaim donor microsegment once tombstones cleared and mark as compacted.

Probabilistic reclamation:
- Each microsegment maintains an LRU-ish decay score derived from access counters and timestamps. During low-load windows, a background worker samples segments probabilistically (bias toward high-frag-score) to avoid centralized compaction storms. Sampling reduces worst-case overhead and spreads memory movement over time.

Integration with batching and runtime scheduler:
- Migration windows scheduled between minibatch dispatches or at controlled throttle rates determined by a dynamic budget (bytes moved/sec) that respects tail-latency SLOs. The scheduler reduces migration throughput when P95 latency or GPU utilization exceed thresholds.
- If migration would interfere with model's critical path, work is demoted to low-priority compute streams and limited to maintaining < X% of device memory bandwidth (configurable).

Data structures and memory layout:
- SegmentMap: dense array of microsegment descriptors (state, free-run metrics, last-access-epoch). Compact metadata stored in 32B per segment.
- RedirectionTable: single-level indirection table per pool, sized by number of active keys. Stored on GPU in pinned memory for atomic updates.
- Tombstone queue: circular buffer of recent migrated physical slots with safe-reclaim-epoch.

Operational knobs:
- segment_size (bytes)
- migration_bandwidth_limit (MB/s)
- sample_rate (segments/sec)
- hot_threshold (access rate to force copy-on-write)
- safe_reclaim_epochs (integer)
- backpressure_latency_cutoff (ms)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation merged to main with feature flag 'soft_migrate_compaction'
KV fragmentation metric (contiguous_free_ratio) improves by >=30% on synthetic churn workload within 24h of runtime compared to baseline
No regression in P95 generation latency >5% under our standard continuous-batching perf tests at 95th percentile load
Percent allocation failures due to fragmentation drops to <0.5% under bursty traffic profile
Telemetry surfaces moved_bytes/sec, compaction_rate, aborted_migrations, and avg_migration_latency
Config knobs documented in runtime ops playbook and Console exposes migration status per-pool
test_plan: Unit tests for SegmentMap and RedirectionTable correctness (atomic flip semantics)
Microbench: synthetic workload with configurable churn to validate fragmentation reduction and moved-bytes budget enforcement
Integration: end-to-end with continuous-batching harness to assert no SLO regressions at multiple load points
Chaos: forcibly inject long-running in-flight requests to validate tombstone safe-reclaim and abort logic
Canary rollout: enable feature flag on small Dedicated pool, monitor telemetry & rollback on guardrail breach
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; unit+integration tests must pass. 2) Canary enable on internal staging fleet (2 nodes) for 48h; watch contiguous_free_ratio and p95 latency. 3) Gradually enable on 10% of Dedicated pools with migration_bandwidth_limit=low for 72h. 4) If stable, increase rollout to 50% then global. 5) Enable Console exposure and Ops runbook after successful global roll. Emergency rollback toggles feature flag and drains in-progress migrations via abort path.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Migration saturates device memory bandwidth and increases tail latency. Mitigation: strict bandwidth limiter and dynamic throttle based on live latency signals.
Risk: Copy-on-write semantics cause transient memory amplification. Mitigation: limit number of concurrent migrations per GPU and prefer compact targets to minimize copies.
Risk: Redirection table update races with request path. Mitigation: atomic pointer flips + epoch-based quiesce; heavy unit tests and formal model checks for atomicity.
Risk: Unanticipated interaction with sharded KV placement across GPUs. Mitigation: perform intra-GPU first; cross-GPU migration only when P2P is available and with extra safety checks.
Risk: Metrics noise hides regressions. Mitigation: baseline dashboards and anomaly alerts focused on migration-related counters.
Risk: Complex ops procedures. Mitigation: ops playbook, one-click rollback, and telemetry that identifies in-flight migrations per pool.

Risk: Security/regulatory concerns for Private deployments when moving customer keys. Mitigation: migrations do not change encryption keys; memory copy remains within secured device VM and follows existing KMS/HSM constraints. Flagged for security review.
